k1.disputed_point: Guidance: the key says 2026 capex is above $25B and 'unchanged in the Q3 letter'. Tesla's Q3 10-Q lowered it to 'in excess of $20 billion'. The key also calls revenue 'in line', but Tesla's own compiled consensus was higher.
k1.why: Electrek's follow-up article of Oct 22, 2026 says the Q3 10-Q, filed Oct 21, changed the wording. It now reads 'to be in excess of $20 billion in 2026', down from 'more than $25 billion' guided since April. The shareholder letter did not contain the change, so the key's 'unchanged in the letter' is true only of the letter. The current guide is still >$20B, not >$25B. A second source, letsdatascience, also reports the cut to about $20B from more than $25B. I could not open the 10-Q's MD&A text to read the sentence directly. On the revenue point, Answers B, C and E cite Tesla's company-compiled consensus of $28.341B against $28.046B reported. I could not open that Tesla page (HTTP 403), so I did not verify it. Other sources put consensus near $28.06B, so 'in line' is defensible, and I'd call the revenue point a 'slight miss or in line' depending on the consensus used. The other key figures (486,532 deliveries, $0.48 vs $0.45 non-GAAP EPS, $787M GAAP net income, $718M operating income) are not contested by the answers, and I did not re-check them.
k1.corrected_answer: Deliveries were 486,532 against company-compiled consensus of about 462k, a beat. Production was 464,391, so inventory fell about 22k. Revenue was about $28.05B, flat year on year and roughly in line with some consensus figures (about $28.06B), though it was slightly below Tesla's company-compiled consensus of $28.34B. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.48 against $0.45 expected. GAAP net income was $787M (-43%), or $0.22 per share. Operating income was $718M (-56%), a 2.6% operating margin. Gross margin was 19.6%. Energy storage deployments were 13.7 GWh against 15.9 GWh consensus, a miss. Regulatory credits fell to $113M. Tesla gives no delivery or revenue guidance. The only hard guide is 2026 capex. The Q3 shareholder letter did not change it, but the Q3 10-Q (filed Oct 21, 2026) lowered it to 'in excess of $20 billion' from 'more than $25 billion'. Nine-month capex was $13.01B.

k2.disputed_point: The 2026 capex guide. The key treats it as still above $25B and says Q4 needs about $12B of capex. Tesla's Q3 10-Q cut the guide to above $20B.
k2.why: Electrek's follow-up article of Oct 22 says the Q3 10-Q now guides to capex "in excess of $20 billion in 2026", down from "more than $25 billion". The earlier Electrek article the key cites (Oct 21) only reflected the old $25B figure, because it was written before the 10-Q was filed. Answers A, B, C, D and E all cite the above-$20B guide from the 10-Q. The key's financial figures check out against Electrek: Q3 capex $4.73B, year-to-date $13.01B, Q3 FCF $1.53B and cash and investments $45.4B. The implied Q4 capex is about $7B to reach the new $20B floor, not $12B. Reaching the old $25B target would have needed roughly $12B. Q4 FCF is therefore still likely negative, but far less dramatically. I opened only the Electrek pages, not the 10-Q itself.
k2.corrected_answer: Cash and investments were $45.4B at the end of Q3. Q3 free cash flow was $1.53B, against -$1.09B in Q2 and $3.99B a year earlier. Q3 capex was $4.73B, and year-to-date capex is $13.01B. The Q3 10-Q cut the 2026 capex guide from more than $25B to more than $20B. Hitting the new floor needs about $7B of capex in Q4, which is above any prior quarter ($2.49B in Q1, $5.79B in Q2, $4.73B in Q3). The old $25B target would have needed about $12B. Expect free cash flow to turn negative in Q4 and cash to fall, though less sharply than under the old guide. I did not verify the debt maturity schedule or rating actions. Check the 10-Q for those. Liquidity is not a near-term stress point.
